target_customer: Chat and video apps needing sticker content (API and SDK buyers), and independent character IP creators who monetize through the platform
problem: Chat apps wanted rich sticker content without building it, and independent sticker artists had no good way to earn from their characters. Stipop later narrowed to a Patreon-like monetization platform for character creators.
business_model: Sticker API and SDK licensing to apps plus creator monetization platform (revenue share)

founders.name: Tony Park
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as co-founder; TechCrunch (2021-08-27) names him as co-founder. Education and prior employers not found in pages opened.

founders.name: Daniel Cho
founders.background_notes: Listed as co-founder on the YC page. Background not found in pages opened.

competitors.name: GIPHY
competitors.what: Sticker and GIF API for messaging apps

competitors.name: Tenor
competitors.what: GIF and sticker search API, owned by Google
competitors.traction_then: Embedded in major keyboards and messengers

technical_complexity.rationale: Search, SDK and content catalog engineering for a small team; no hard research problems.

defensibility.rationale: Creator catalog of about 250K stickers gave some supply side pull, but Giphy and Tenor had free distribution and the content is easy to replicate.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents were already giving stickers away inside major apps. Stipop later moved away from the sticker business toward creator monetization.

market_need_then: Chat apps competed on expressive features and stickers drive engagement, especially in Asia. Stipop reported customers such as Canva, Teams, Google and Adobe using its stickers.

branding.domain_note: Uses stipop.io (studio.stipop.io for the creator product); acquisition history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Fun and creator friendly, pitched as Patreon for character creators

branding.community_and_virality: Founders interviewed by TechCrunch (2021-08-27) and other outlets; Stipop was the first Korean company in Snap's Yellow accelerator per profile sources.

brand_strength.rationale: Little brand press beyond funding and accelerator coverage; the name suggests stickers, which the pivot moved away from.

pivots.from: Sticker platform and sticker API and SDK for chat apps
pivots.why: Not stated by a source; the YC page says it previously was a sticker platform.

outcome_analysis: Stipop is still listed as active with 8 people. It was backed by Snap's Yellow accelerator and YC but no later priced round is found. It faced free incumbents in Giphy and Tenor and pivoted from stickers to creator monetization, so the story is a stalled early stage company rather than a clear success or failure.
notes: Funding: Seedtable lists a 1.3M pre-Series A in 2020-11 from SEMA Translink, Snap, Lotte Accelerator and Strong Ventures, and CB Insights lists 1.95M over 7 rounds; both are aggregators with differing labels, so unverified and not recorded as rounds. No Series A found. Founder education and employers not found. The company site and a founder interview could not be fetched (domain safety check rate-limited).
